_comment: The county record score (scripts/county_record_score.py): how restrictive a county is for wind, solar and battery storage, read from its own published record rather than from its resemblance to other counties. Hand-edited; no process writes it. Added 2026-10-21 after the October 16 case studies scored Linn County, IA (two contested solar projects approved, rules in force no stricter than severity 2) above Nicholas County, KY and Cherokee County, KS (each with a moratorium in force). The resemblance score (config/county_model_registration.json) is kept, unchanged, as the profile prior for counties with no record. Like that score, this one is internal: nothing on a page or in a county report reads it without a separate decision by Price.

instruments._note: Points for one restriction instrument (rows sharing an instrument_id are one instrument; its severity is the highest of its rows). Points = severity points x currency x jurisdiction x technology breadth.
instruments._currency_note: unknown is the share of status-unknown instruments found in force by the 2026-10-21 status sample (60 NREL instruments, seeded and stratified by technology and severity, two readers each): 40 of the 47 settled were in force, 89 percent weighted by group size; counting the 4 whose record matched no adopted instrument as not in force gives about 78 percent. 0.85 lies between the two.

jurisdiction._note: A county-wide instrument governs the whole county; a city, town, township or village instrument governs part of it.

instruments._others_note: A county's instrument points are its largest instrument's points plus others_weight times the sum of the rest, so a second and third instrument add to the score without a long list of minor rules outweighing one moratorium.

projects._note: Contested projects placed in the county, by outcome. A confirmed outcome counts fully, a recorded but unconfirmed one half. Approvals lower the score: a county that has approved contested projects is shown to be open under its rules.
projects._approval_note: Approvals can take off at most this share of the county's instrument and zoning points, and never take the score below the points of a severity 4 county-wide instrument in force: a moratorium in force outweighs earlier approvals.

zoning_transition._note: In these states a county without zoning has no local permit over a wind or solar project (state_policies.csv: the county is the siting authority, through planning and zoning, and no state body sites these projects). A county that moves from no zoning to zoning while projects are proposed is setting up the means to restrict them, so the move counts as a county-wide instrument at the severity below, in force from the date drafting began until counts_for_years_after_adoption after the code is adopted.

counties.summary: Cherokee County has no zoning. A consultant (Confluence) is drafting its first zoning code for the county planning commission, under a draft comprehensive plan that lists wind farms, solar farms, battery storage and data centers as high-impact uses and records that many residents supported prohibiting them or regulating them strictly.

sources.what: draft comprehensive plan (Confluence), with the October 2025 workshop results

counties.summary: Bourbon County has no county zoning. In June 2026 the commission adopted a 365-day moratorium on utility-scale power generation and other uses and chose Confluence to write its comprehensive plan and zoning regulations; on September 16, 2026 it approved a $116,500 agreement for the county's first plan and zoning code, which is to cover wind, solar, battery storage and data centers.
counties.review: Hand-entered on 2026-10-21 from the Kansas zoning pass (one research reading per county, no second reading). Not yet a review row.

counties.summary: Brown County had no general county zoning. After a January 10, 2025 planning commission hearing, the county commission adopted a limited zoning regulation in February 2025 that prohibits commercial wind projects of 500 kW or more in the unincorporated county outside three city areas; a solar amendment followed in October 2025 and data center and battery storage rules in August 2026.

sources.what: county FAQ: a zoned county whose only restriction applies to commercial wind (read)

counties.review: Hand-entered on 2026-10-21 from the Kansas zoning pass (one research reading per county, no second reading). Not yet a review row.

counties.summary: Crawford County zoned only a southeast part of the county from 1967; the rest of its unincorporated land had no zoning. After moratoriums on wind, solar, battery storage and other uses, the commission approved zoning of all unincorporated land and a ban on future wind projects on July 10, 2026 (Motions 26-319 and 26-320). Counted here as a transition because most of the county moved from no zoning to zoning.

countywide zoning approved, no new wind farms (read)

counties.summary: Kiowa County has no zoning. Commissioners began discussing zoning in April 2026 and on October 5, 2026 voted 3-0 to issue a request for proposals for planning and zoning services, with a public meeting on zoning set for November 17, 2026. The minutes do not name wind, solar or storage as a reason; an Invenergy project was before the commission over the same period.

On July 8, 2024 the commission voted 2-1 for Resolution 2024-24-L, zoning the unincorporated county outside the Parsons area from July 12, 2024; the commissioners' press release says they chose zoning to regulate industrial wind and solar companies.

counties.summary: Nemaha County had no county zoning and approved the Soldier Creek wind farm by agreements in 2020. It created a planning commission in 2020, adopted a comprehensive plan in 2023, and on July 6, 2026 the commission adopted a countywide land development code 2-1, after adding electrical and battery storage facilities to the uses that need a conditional use permit.

build_out._note: Plants built without a recorded fight are uncontested approvals: the record holds only the projects that drew opposition, so without these a county that approved everything quietly looks the same as one never asked. Counted from EIA-860M (one source, so no plant twice): solar, wind or battery storage plants of at least min_mw, operating or under construction, whose year (online, or planned online) is since_year or later and no earlier than the year of the county's latest instrument in force, so a plant that predates a rule is not read as that rule's approval. A county's contested projects that advanced are assumed to be among its plants, so only plants beyond that number count. Each counts as the 'built' outcome in projects.points, inside the same approval caps.

no_county_zoning._note: States whose counties have no general zoning power, so no county can adopt a siting rule for unincorporated land; only its cities can, inside their limits. In these states an empty record is evidence in itself: the county government cannot restrict, so a county with no record is weighed at evidence_weight.no_county_zoning against its profile prior instead of being scored on the prior alone. Each state names the verified state_policies.csv row that says so.

evidence_weight._note: How far the record speaks for itself. combined = weight x record points + (1 - weight) x profile points, where profile points are the mean record points of all counties in the same decile of the resemblance score, a county with no record counting as zero (a floor, since most counties have never been examined). A county with no record and no negative check is scored on its profile alone.

tiers.name: closed
tiers.label: Closed: a moratorium or ban in force, or rules that act as one, county-wide

tiers.name: severe
tiers.label: Severe: rules likely to block most projects

tiers.name: restrictive
tiers.label: Restrictive: material rules, or blocked projects

tiers.name: regulated
tiers.label: Regulated but open: rules in force, projects approved under them

reference_counties._note: The counties of the October 16 case studies, printed in the report so a change to the rubric shows its effect on them. The October 2026 review of the four reports read Nicholas and Cherokee as much less friendly than Linn.
